intro.setting: Six branches to cover, a long weekend coming, and a busy area manager

playbook.title: The {{company.name}} Playbook
rules: If you can undo a decision before your next visit, take a decision.
Never commit the company to anything beyond this month without approval.
Your area manager is busy. Every call takes a day.
Retailers are partners. Tell them the truth about what we can deliver.

decisions.situation: The shelf labels still show last month's higher price, not this week's promotion. You have promo labels in the car.

facilitator.note: Plain two-way door. Nobody should escalate this. Deferring costs a day because you have to come back.

options.label: Swap the labels now with the store staff
options.immediate: Ten minutes with a staff member and the shelf is right. Shoppers can see the deal.

deferred.headline: {{branches.alNahda}} shoppers snap up juice promotion
deferred.standfirst: Correct shelf pricing drove a strong weekend for the promotion.

grade.rationale: Yours to fix, and fixed on the spot.

options.label: Mention it to the store manager and move on
options.immediate: The manager says he'll sort it. On your next visit, the old labels are still up.

deferred.headline: Juice promotion goes unnoticed at {{branches.alNahda}}
deferred.standfirst: Shoppers saw the old price for most of the promotion.

grade.rationale: A ten-minute fix left undone all week.

options.label: Call your area manager
options.immediate: Your area manager sounds confused. "Why are you calling me about labels? Just fix them." You fix them, a day later than you could have.

deferred.headline: Area manager: "Please stop calling me about labels"
deferred.standfirst: The promotion was fixed in the end, a day late.

grade.rationale: Yours to fix. The call only added a day.

decisions.situation: The store manager offers you the end-of-aisle display this weekend, if {{company.name}} gives an extra 5% off.

facilitator.note: Looks two-way (one weekend only), but a discount sets a precedent that's hard to take back. Both doors cost the same. This is a debate door.

options.label: Accept, for this weekend only
options.immediate: You shake on it. The display goes up on Thursday night.

deferred.headline: {{branches.muwaileh}} manager asks for 5% again, and two other branches want the same
deferred.standfirst: A great weekend on the end-cap, but the one-off discount is now the expected price.

grade.rationale: A judgment call. We'll discuss this one.

options.label: Decline, and offer the standard promotion instead
options.immediate: The manager shrugs. "Your loss." The display goes to someone else.

deferred.headline: Rival brand takes {{branches.muwaileh}} end-cap for the long weekend
deferred.standfirst: A quieter weekend for {{company.name}}, but pricing stays where it was.

grade.rationale: A judgment call. We'll discuss this one.

options.label: Call your area manager
options.immediate: "Your call, but be careful what you set up." By the time you call back, the display has gone to a competitor.

deferred.headline: Rival brand takes {{branches.muwaileh}} end-cap while {{company.name}} deliberates
deferred.standfirst: The decision came back to the rep anyway, a day too late.

grade.rationale: Your manager had already said it was your call.

decisions.situation: Your juice has been moved to the bottom shelf, not where the agreed shelf plan puts it.

facilitator.note: Restoring the agreed plan is the rep's job. Clear two-way door.

options.label: Put it back where the plan says, with the staff's OK
options.immediate: Back at eye level in twenty minutes. The staff didn't mind.

deferred.headline: Juice back at eye level, {{branches.alMajaz}} sales recover
deferred.standfirst: Sales returned to normal within the week.

grade.rationale: Restoring the agreed shelf plan is your job.

options.label: Note it for your next visit
options.immediate: You log it and move on. On your next visit, it's still on the bottom shelf.

deferred.headline: A week on the bottom shelf costs {{branches.alMajaz}} juice sales
deferred.standfirst: Shoppers didn't find what they couldn't see.

grade.rationale: A twenty-minute fix left undone all week.

options.label: Call your area manager
options.immediate: "That's literally your job." You move it back, a day later than you could have.

deferred.headline: Area manager's week interrupted by shelf question
deferred.standfirst: The shelf was fixed in the end, a day late.

grade.rationale: Yours to fix. The call only added a day.

decisions.situation: The chain's buyer for three branches offers to drop a competitor's juice completely, if {{company.name}} commits to exclusive supply at a fixed price for 12 months.

facilitator.note: Clear one-way door. Calling is the right move, and the only place in the game where it clearly is. Teaches that escalation belongs at one-way doors.

options.label: Agree on the spot. It's a huge win
options.immediate: The buyer is delighted. You shake hands and he says he'll send the paperwork.

deferred.headline: {{company.name}} hit with penalties after summer exclusivity deal
deferred.standfirst: The factory couldn't guarantee summer supply at the fixed price the rep agreed.

grade.rationale: A 12-month commitment is never a one-person decision.

options.label: Decline. It's above your level
options.immediate: You thank the buyer and say no. He looks surprised, and says he'll talk to other suppliers.

deferred.headline: Rival juice brand wins exclusive deal at three {{chain.name}} branches
deferred.standfirst: An opportunity nobody at {{company.name}} got to consider.

grade.rationale: Saying no alone closed a door nobody else got to look at.

options.label: Call your area manager
options.immediate: Your area manager takes it straight to the commercial team. It costs you a day, but the deal is in the right hands.

deferred.headline: {{company.name}} signs three-branch deal on terms the factory can meet
deferred.standfirst: Commercial restructured the offer before signing.

grade.rationale: Exactly the kind of decision to take to your manager.

decisions.situation: A competitor is handing out free samples next to your shelf. You could run your own tasting this Saturday, but it would use half your sampling budget for the whole quarter.

facilitator.note: Money spent can't come back (one-way), but the amount is small. Both doors cost the same. Debate door.

options.label: Run the tasting
options.immediate: You book a promoter for Saturday. The tasting table goes up by the entrance.

deferred.headline: Saturday tasting wins {{branches.alRashidiya}}, but Q3 launch has no sampling budget left
deferred.standfirst: A strong weekend now, a thinner launch later.

grade.rationale: A judgment call. We'll discuss this one.

options.label: Save the budget
options.immediate: You let the competitor have the weekend. Your budget stays intact.

deferred.headline: Competitor tasting wins the weekend at {{branches.alRashidiya}}
deferred.standfirst: {{company.name}} keeps its sampling budget for the Q3 launch.

grade.rationale: A judgment call. We'll discuss this one.

options.label: Call your area manager
options.immediate: "It's your budget." By the time you've called back, there's no promoter available for Saturday.

deferred.headline: Competitor tasting wins the weekend while {{company.name}} waits
deferred.standfirst: The budget was saved, mostly by default.

decisions.situation: The chain's category manager emails you. She wants written confirmation that the current promotional price will hold until the end of the year.

facilitator.note: Looks easy (it's the price we already have), but it's a written commitment beyond this month: a one-way door. The playbook covers it (rule 2), so declining yourself is fine and calling isn't needed.

options.label: Reply yes. It's the price we already have
options.immediate: You reply in two lines. She thanks you and files it.

deferred.headline: Price U-turn row: {{chain.namePlural}} forwards rep's email to {{company.name}} commercial
deferred.standfirst: {{company.name}} raised prices in October. The buyer had it in writing that they wouldn't.

grade.rationale: A written promise beyond this month, made alone.

options.label: Reply that promotional prices are set monthly, so you can't confirm beyond that
options.immediate: She's a little annoyed, but thanks you for being straight with her.

deferred.headline: Monthly pricing holds at {{chain.namePlural}} despite buyer grumbles
deferred.standfirst: No surprises when prices changed in October.

grade.rationale: Honest, and within what you're allowed to promise.

options.label: Call your area manager
options.immediate: Your area manager replies to her with exactly what the playbook says. It costs you a day.

deferred.headline: Monthly pricing holds at {{chain.namePlural}} after manager steps in
deferred.standfirst: The same answer the rep could have given a day earlier.

grade.rationale: The right answer, but the playbook had already given it to you.

reveal.title: One month later
reveal.dateline: Sharjah & Ajman edition, one month on

chrome.managerHeading: Your decisions and your manager's review of them
chrome.managerSubhead: This is your manager's read, based on the company's field playbook.
chrome.closing: When you are ready, return to the main workshop room ↗
chrome.joinTeamCallout: Discuss each choice before you confirm. Once you pick a door, you cannot undo it.

tooSlow.name: Too slow
tooSlow.zero: Nothing waited that was yours to decide.
tooSlow.withBranches: Waited on decisions that were yours: {stops}.

tooFast.name: Too fast
tooFast.zero: Nothing went ahead that needed a check.

operator.name: The Navigator
operator.description: You moved fast on what you could undo, and slowed down on what you couldn't.
operator.hover: Navigators move fast on what they can undo, and slow down on what they can't.

escalator.name: The Escalator
escalator.description: You kept things safe by checking in, even when the call was yours to make.
escalator.hover: Escalators keep things safe by checking in, even when the call is theirs to make.
escalator.tip: Where the decision is easy and cheap to reverse, just take it.

cowboy.name: The Sprinter
cowboy.description: You kept things moving, including promises that weren't yours to make.
cowboy.hover: Sprinters keep things moving, including promises that aren't theirs to make.
cowboy.tip: If you couldn't undo it before the next visit, pause and bring someone in.

bottleneck.name: The Bottleneck
bottleneck.description: You held back on the small calls and rushed the big ones.
bottleneck.hover: Bottlenecks hold back on the small calls and rush the big ones.
bottleneck.tip: Take the easy reversals on the spot. Slow down only when you couldn't undo it.

ui.weekBoth: You waited on decisions that were yours to make. But went ahead with some that needed a check.
ui.weekSlow: You waited on decisions that were yours to make.
ui.weekFast: You went ahead with some that needed a check.
ui.weekClear: Nothing waited that was yours to decide, and nothing went ahead that needed a check.
